The World Health Organization's Department of Child and Adolescent Health in Geneva published a report in 2001 focusing on the relationship between maternal health and child outcomes. 2. Karaarslan BT conducted a master's thesis in 2002 at Hacettepe University, evaluating the impact of home-based early intervention programs on the developmental progress of very low birth weight premature infants. 3. Kemper KJ and Babonis TR, in 1992, explored the importance of screening for maternal depression in pediatric clinics, as published in the American Journal of Diseases of Children. 4. Knight JR and colleagues developed a curriculum for pediatric residents under the Bright Futures initiative, as detailed in Ambulatory Pediatrics in 2001. 5. Kotchabhakdi NJ highlighted the innovative use of video for early child health and education in Thailand, as reported in the Development Communication Report in 1993. 6. Lamb ME reviewed the effects of nonparental childcare on child development, providing an update in the Canadian Journal of Psychiatry in August 1996. 7. Lambrechts T, Bryce J, and Orinda V summarized the initial experiences with the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) strategy in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 1999. 8. Larsen JJ and Juhasz AM developed the Knowledge of Child Development Inventory, which was published in Adolescence in 1986. 9. MacDonald-Clark NJ and Harney-Boffman JL examined the use of NCAST and HOME tools in assessing minority populations, specifically Alaska Eskimos, as published in Pediatric Nursing in 1994. 10. MacPhee D created the Knowledge of Infant Development Inventory and cataloged prior experiences with infants in a 1981 publication from Princeton, NJ. 11. McCarthy P and colleagues investigated mother-child interactions and clinical judgment during acute pediatric illnesses, as reported in the Journal of Pediatrics in 2000. 12. McCarthy PL et al. conducted a randomized trial on the Acute Illness Observation Scales to assess mothers' clinical judgment, published in the Journal of Pediatrics in 1990. 13. McCarthy PL et al. developed observation scales to identify serious illnesses in febrile children, as detailed in Pediatrics in 1982. 14. McLearn KT et al. introduced the Healthy Steps approach to child development and pediatrics for the 21st century, as published in the Journal of Urban Health in 1998. 15. Minkovitz C and the Healthy Steps Evaluation Team assessed the early effects of the Healthy Steps for Young Children Program, as reported in the Archives of Pediatric and Adolescent Medicine in 2001. 16. Moszynski P reported in BMJ in 2004 that girls in southern Sudan are more likely to die in childbirth than to complete primary school. 17. Murray L et al. conducted a controlled trial on the shortand long-term effects of psychological treatment for postpartum depression, focusing on its impact on the mother-child relationship and child outcomes, as published in the British Journal of Psychiatry in 2003. 18. Murray L et al. examined the cognitive development of 5-year-old children born to postnatally depressed mothers, as detailed in the Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry in 1996. 19. Needleman R et al. implemented a clinic-based intervention to promote literacy, as published in the American Journal of Diseases of Children in 1991. 20. Needleman R and Silverstein M reviewed the evidence supporting pediatric interventions to encourage reading aloud, as reported in the Journal of Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics in 2004. 21. Ninio A explored maternal attitudes and the naive theory of infants in two subgroups in Israel, as published in Child Development in 1979. 22. Nishimura M et al. investigated the relationships between child development and home environment at 1, 8, and 14 months of age in Japan. 23. Nobile C and Drotar D reviewed research on the quality of parent-provider communication in pediatric care, offering implications and recommendations in the Journal of Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics in 2003. 24. Ohya Y et al. studied psychosocial factors influencing adherence to treatment advice in childhood atopic dermatitis, as published in the Journal of Investigative Dermatology in 2001. 25. Olness K discussed the global epidemic of brain development impairments leading to cognitive deficits, as detailed in the Journal of Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics in 2003. 26.
